inspiration.observed_pattern: A product report uses AVG(DISTINCT ...) to average only unique product prices instead of counting repeated prices multiple times.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an original regional pricing report. A LEFT JOIN groups decimal prices by region and projects ordinary AVG, AVG(DISTINCT), and COUNT(DISTINCT) together; duplicate prices, NULL prices, and a region with no products make the distinct-average and NULL aggregate behavior observable without copying the source schema or rows.

fixture_notes: Region 10 has prices 100.00, 100.00, 160.00, and NULL, so ordinary AVG is 120.00 while AVG(DISTINCT) is 130.00. Region 20 has two distinct non-NULL prices and one NULL; region 30 has no products and must retain NULL aggregate results through the LEFT JOIN.
determinism_notes: Region IDs and product IDs are fixed; the grouped report is ordered by the unique region ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE sales_regions (region_id INT PRIMARY KEY, region_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE regional_prices (product_id INT PRIMARY KEY, region_id INT NOT NULL, product_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, list_price DECIMAL(10,2) NULL)

INSERT INTO regional_prices VALUES (1, 10, 'starter', 100.00), (2, 10, 'standard', 100.00), (3, 10, 'premium', 160.00), (4, 10, 'custom', NULL), (5, 20, 'starter', 200.00), (6, 20, 'premium', 260.00), (7, 20, 'custom', NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT r.region_id, r.region_name, AVG(p.list_price) AS average_price, AVG(DISTINCT p.list_price) AS distinct_average_price, COUNT(DISTINCT p.list_price) AS distinct_price_points FROM sales_regions r LEFT JOIN regional_prices p ON p.region_id = r.region_id GROUP BY r.region_id, r.region_name ORDER BY r.region_id
